extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: A 1.2-million-example open-source supervised fine-tuning (SFT) reasoning dataset consisting of 850k math, 250k code, and 100k science question-response pairs with reasoning traces distilled from QwQ-32B.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, Hritik Bansal, Marianna Nezhurina, Jean Mercat, Trung Vu, Zayne Sprague, Ashima Suvama, Benjamin Feuer, Liangyu Chen, Zaid Khan, Eric Frankel, Sachin Grover, Caroline Choi, Niklas Muennighoff, Shiye Su, Wanjia Zhao, John Yang, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Kartik Sharma, Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji, Yichuan Deng, Sarah Pratt, Vivek Ramanujan, Jon Saad-Falcon, Jeffrey Li, Achal Dave, Alon Albalak, Kushal Arora, Blake Wulfe, Chinmay Hegde, Greg Durrett, Sewoong Oh, Mohit Bansal, Saadia Gabriel, Aditya Grover, Kai-Wei Chang, Vaishaal Shankar, Aaron Gokaslan, Mike A. Merrill, Tatsunori Hashimoto, Yejin Choi, Jenia Jitsev, Reinhard Heckel, Maheswaran Sathiamoorthy, Alexandros G. Dimakis, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were sourced from selected high-performing question sources (OpenMath-2-Math for math, StackExchange CodeGolf and OpenCodeReasoning for code, and StackExchange Physics and an Organic Chemistry PDF extraction pipeline for science). Questions were filtered using LLMs, exact deduplicated (math and science), randomly sampled to target counts, and expanded by sampling 16 answers per question from the teacher model QwQ-32B.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: OpenMath-2-Math, StackExchange CodeGolf, OpenCodeReasoning, StackExchange Physics, and organic chemistry textbooks/PDFs (including SCP-116K).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Question filtering was applied using difficulty-based selection via GPT-4o-mini for code and response length selection via GPT-4.1-mini for math and science. Decontamination was performed against benchmark datasets by removing training samples with normalized Indel similarity of 75% or higher or matching 13-grams. Exact deduplication was applied to math and science questions using normalized Indel similarity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Exact deduplication on questions for math and science, decontamination against evaluation benchmarks (AIME24, AMC23, MATH500, CodeElo, CodeForces, LiveCodeBench, GPQA Diamond, JEEBench, HMMT, HLE) using normalized Indel similarity (75% threshold) and 13-gram overlap, and formatting into prompt-response reasoning format using <think> and </think> tags.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Responses and chain-of-thought reasoning traces were generated by prompting the QwQ-32B teacher model 16 times per question. No post-hoc answer filtering was applied to the final dataset recipe based on ablation studies showing answer filtering did not outperform retaining all generated answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Extensive ablation experiments analyzed answer filtering approaches including majority consensus, LLM judge verification, FastText classification, and response length selection. Results indicated that no answer filtering method outperformed the baseline of retaining all generated answers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Evaluation showed that supervised fine-tuning on reasoning datasets without explicit safety-tuning or alignment data inadvertently degrades model safety alignment, leading to higher harmfulness rates on Harmbench and increased over-refusal on XSTEST.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The study does not explore reinforcement learning datasets or staged SFT / curriculum learning. In addition, distilled reasoning models continue to suffer from generalization deficits on task perturbations (such as Alice in Wonderland variations) and safety alignment degradation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and distillation for training large language models on complex reasoning tasks across mathematics, coding, and science.
